Visit note | 2026-05-24 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Marium Sheikh, 81, female. Mrs. Sheikh returns for review reporting that she feels numbness in her toes, burning in both feet, and a tingling sensation like pins and needles. She is a shopkeeper, and she mentions that these symptoms have become worse since walking barefoot at home in Uttara. She takes no regular medications and has no other major illnesses. On examination, there is reduced sensation at 8 of 10 monofilament test sites. Other vitals show BP 122/75 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 89 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and muscle strength is normal in both lower limbs. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to check her feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep her blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.
